literal: Within a month he was buried; pleas for posthumous offices were not granted.
idiomatic: He was buried within the month; no posthumous offices were granted despite entreaties.

literal: He had his own mourning carriage made without carved ornament—only hemp tassels and cord netting.
idiomatic: He designed his own hearse: no carving, only hemp tassels and rope mesh.

literal: Bright vessels and the like were not permitted at all.
idiomatic: Grave goods and bright vessels were forbidden entirely.

literal: Yu had long served in the central offices, skilled in records and registers; in office he judged cases, swift as flowing water.
idiomatic: Yu had long served in the capital, expert in ledgers and registers; on the bench his rulings ran swift as water.

literal: Yet by nature he was treacherous and jealous, shallow in friendship and duty.
idiomatic: Yet he was treacherous and jealous by nature, shallow in friendship and loyalty.

literal: Outwardly he seemed square and ruled; inwardly he was inconstant.
idiomatic: Outwardly he looked square and stern; inwardly he was restless.

literal: He accepted bribes, bent reason and twisted law, harsh in wording and cruel—many were harmed.
idiomatic: He took bribes, bent law to favor, piled on harsh charges—many were ruined.

literal: Gentlemen feared and hated him.
idiomatic: Men of standing feared and loathed him.

literal: Lady Zhang, concubine of Prince of Dongping Yuan Kuang of Wei, was dissolute and unrestrained.
idiomatic: Lady Zhang, concubine to Wei's Prince of Dongping Yuan Kuang, was wanton and unbridled.

literal: Yu at first committed adultery with her, then took her as wife.
idiomatic: Yu first lay with her in secret, then made her his wife.

literal: Beguiled by her slanders, he cast off his former wife of the Yu clan, unwilling toward his son Yun.
idiomatic: He heeded her slanders, cast off his first wife of the Yu house, and turned cold to his son Yun.

literal: The household seethed within; they reported one another in rivalry, and he was deeply scorned by the world.
idiomatic: His kin seethed and denounced one another; the world held him in deep contempt.

literal: Posthumously granted Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Opening the Government with Three Excellencies' ceremonial rank, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Qing.

literal: Posthumous title: Majestic and Reverent.
idiomatic: Posthumous title: Majestic and Reverent.

literal: His son Yun succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Yun succeeded.

literal: Wei Yuan, styled Gourou, was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Wei Yuan, styled Gourou, came from Dai.

literal: For generations his house was a great clan.
idiomatic: His clan had been a great house for generations.

literal: His father Mukin was famed in his day for courage and strategy and held the post of Administrator of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: His father Mukin was famed for courage and stratagem and served as Administrator of Zhongshan.

literal: Yuan was famed for skill in archery and was made Gentleman of the Feathered Forest; for tireless diligence he won notice.
idiomatic: Yuan was known for archery and made Gentleman of the Feathered Forest; tireless service won him notice.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Master of Carriages attendant and enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng.
idiomatic: He rose to Master of Carriages attendant and was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng.

literal: In the Heping era he was transferred to Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan and advanced to Marquis of Taichang.
idiomatic: In the Heping era he became Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan and was advanced to Marquis of Taichang.

literal: In Tian'an year 1, Xue Andu of Song surrendered Xu Province to the court; Emperor Xiaowen made Yuan bearer of the staff of authority and commander of military affairs on the eastern route, and he went with Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong.
idiomatic: In Tian'an 1 Xue Andu of Song surrendered Xu Province; Emperor Xiaowen made Yuan bearer of the staff and eastern-route commander, and he set out with Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong.

literal: Bi Zhongjing, Governor of Yan Province in Song, sent Administrator of Dongping Zhang Chouyi to submit; Yuan received them all and drove forward at length.
idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing, Song's Governor of Yan, sent Dongping's administrator Zhang Chouyi to submit; Yuan took them in and pressed on at length.

literal: Song sent generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi and others to encamp at the approaches to Xiapi.
idiomatic: Song sent Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, and others to camp at the Xiapi approaches.

literal: Andu came out of the city to see Yuan.
idiomatic: Andu came out of the city to meet Yuan.

literal: Yuan, following court orders, appointed him Governor of Xu Province and sent Secretariat Attendant Gao Lu, Li Can, and others back into the city with Andu.
idiomatic: Yuan, per the court's order, made Andu Governor of Xu and sent Secretariat Attendants Gao Lu and Li Can into the city with him.

literal: He separately ordered Kong Bogong to reassure Andu inside and out, and only then did Yuan enter Pengcheng.
idiomatic: He left Kong Bogong to steady Andu within and without, then entered Pengcheng himself.

literal: Because Yong still held strategic ground, Yuan ordered Andu and Can to defend together.
idiomatic: Yong still held the choke points, so Yuan had Andu and Can hold the city together.

literal: He himself led crack troops, raised banners without, struck Liangcheng in divisions, and cut their grain route.
idiomatic: He led picked troops abroad, struck Liangcheng in detachments, and severed their grain line.

literal: Yong thereupon abandoned the city and fled by night.
idiomatic: Yong abandoned the city and fled by night.

literal: Thereupon he sent Gao Lu and Zhang Tan as paired Governors of Eastern Xu Province;
idiomatic: He then paired Gao Lu with Zhang Tan as Governors of Eastern Xu;

literal: Li Can and Bi Zhongjing as paired Governors of Eastern Yan Province.
idiomatic: and Li Can with Bi Zhongjing as Governors of Eastern Yan.

literal: Yuan was appointed Opening the Government, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Xu Province, and Duke of Huaiyang.
idiomatic: Yuan was made Opening the Government, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Xu, and Duke of Huaiyang.

literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was summoned as Grand Steward of the Inner Court.
idiomatic: At the opening of Taihe he was summoned as Grand Steward of the Inner Court.

literal: Shortly after he went out as bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Guards the West, Opening the Government, and Commander-in-Chief at Tongwan—he won the hearts of the barbarians.
idiomatic: Soon he went out as bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Guards the West, Opening the Government, and commander at Tongwan, and won the tribes' hearts.

literal: In year 3 he was advanced to Prince of Huaiyang; as an elder of long standing he was honored, permitted a palanquin and staff in court.
idiomatic: In year 3 he was made Prince of Huaiyang; as a veteran he was honored with a palanquin and staff at court.

literal: After Emperor Gao of Qi was established, he sent many spies to stir the newly submitted;
idiomatic: After Gao of Qi took the throne, he sent spies to stir the new subjects;

literal: malcontents rose everywhere like wasps.
idiomatic: and malcontents swarmed up everywhere.

literal: Because Yuan's prestige had long resounded, he was sent to command all armies to suppress them.
idiomatic: Yuan's name had long carried; he was sent to command all armies against them.

literal: The southeast was pacified; far and near submitted.
idiomatic: The southeast was cleared; far and near lay quiet.

literal: He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Department of State Affairs, transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing, and advanced to Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Department of State Affairs, became Director of the Masters of Writing, and rose to Minister of Works.

literal: In year 10, by precedent the princely surname was reduced to commoner rank; he was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang Commandery.
idiomatic: In year 10, by precedent princely houses were reduced to common rank; he was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang.

literal: That year he repeatedly memorialized that age compelled retirement; the edict permitted it.
idiomatic: That year he repeatedly begged to retire on account of age; the edict allowed it.

literal: Yuan came to court to thank him for release and was received in the hall;
idiomatic: Yuan came to court to thank the emperor for release and was received in the hall;

literal: ordered to ascend the hall for a feast of honor; granted a dark cap and plain robes.
idiomatic: ordered up the hall for a feast of honor and given a dark cap and plain robes.

literal: Another edict said: "Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan, Duke of Shanyang Commandery, and former Grand Herald You Minggen, Marquis of Xintai—both possess the four virtues of the Changes, bright trust and plain sincerity, ranks eminent at the terrace stars, returning in old age to private dwellings.
idiomatic: Another edict read: "Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan of Shanyang and former Grand Herald You Minggen of Xintai—both embody the four virtues of the Changes, bright in trust and plain in heart, eminent at court, now retiring to their homes.

literal: They may be called to know the beginning and know the end—worthies rare in an age."
idiomatic: They know the start and the finish—worthies rare in their time."

literal: Sir, at eighty years, should occupy the weight of the three elders;
idiomatic: Sir, at eighty, should bear the weight of the three elders;

literal: Minister, at seventy years, may fill the choice of the five elders."
idiomatic: Minister, at seventy, may serve among the five elders."

literal: Thereupon the three elders and five elders were nurtured in the Bright Hall, the state elders and common elders on the steps below.
idiomatic: Then the three elders and five elders were honored in the Bright Hall, state and common elders on the steps below.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen bowed twice to the three elders, bared his shoulder and cut the victim himself, held the cup and fed them;
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen bowed twice to the three elders, bared shoulder and cut the victim himself, held the cup and fed them;

literal: toward the five elders he performed the bow of respect;
idiomatic: to the five elders he performed the bow of respect;

literal: robes were granted to state elders and common elders in graded measure.
idiomatic: robes were granted to state and common elders by rank.

literal: Then Yuan said: "Since heaven and earth were divided and the Five Agents operated their laws, what men revere—none is weightier than filial obedience.
idiomatic: Yuan then said: "Since heaven and earth split and the Five Agents ran their course, nothing men honor weighs more than filial piety.

literal: Yet the five filial acts and six harmonies are what the realm puts first; I pray Your Majesty will weight them to transform the four quarters.
idiomatic: The five filial acts and six harmonies lead the realm; I pray Your Majesty will weight them to transform the four quarters.

literal: I am already aged and do not probe distant ends; what heart and ear reach, I dare not withhold sincerity.
idiomatic: I am old and cannot see far; what heart and ear reach, I dare not withhold truth.

literal: The emperor said: "The way of filial obedience is the warp of heaven and earth.
idiomatic: The emperor said: "Filial obedience is the warp of heaven and earth.

literal: Now receiving the three elders' clear words, I inscribe them in my breast."
idiomatic: Now I receive the three elders' clear words and inscribe them in my breast."

literal: Minggen said: "Utmost filial piety penetrates spirits; utmost harmony moves the unseen—hence the Odes: 'When filial piety and fraternal duty reach their height, they communicate with spirits and gods and shine across the four seas.'
idiomatic: Minggen said: "Utmost filial piety moves spirits; utmost harmony touches the unseen—the Odes say: 'When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their height, they reach spirits and gods and shine across the four seas.'

literal: Thus the way of filial obedience has nowhere it does not reach.
idiomatic: So filial obedience leaves nowhere untouched.

literal: I pray Your Majesty will keep it in mind to succor the black-haired people.
idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will keep it in mind to succor the people.

literal: My years are decayed timber, my insight dim; in foolish counsel alone I dare not spare effort.
idiomatic: My years are rotten timber, my sight dim; in foolish counsel I dare not spare effort.

literal: The emperor said: "The five elders assist the three elders in speaking the highest pattern and spreading virtuous words.
idiomatic: The emperor said: "The five elders aid the three elders in speaking the highest pattern and spreading virtue.

literal: I shall constrain myself and restore ritual, to carry what you impart."
idiomatic: I shall restrain myself and restore ritual, to carry what you teach."

literal: When the rites were finished, they were granted one palanquin.
idiomatic: When the rites ended, each was granted a palanquin.

literal: An edict said: "Honoring elders and esteeming the five elders, the sacred kings shared this aim; revering years and honoring virtue, sages through the ages held one track.
idiomatic: An edict said: "Honoring elders and esteeming the five elders—the sacred kings shared this; revering years and honoring virtue—sages through the ages held one path.

literal: Though my way falls short of the dark wind and my insight is dim to the bright pattern, yet I look up to receive earlier instructions and bend my steps to follow their intent.
idiomatic: Though my way falls short of the dark wind and my sight is dim to the bright pattern, I look up to earlier teaching and bend my steps to follow it.

literal: Therefore I exalt the aged through virtue and establish the five elders through primacy;
idiomatic: So I exalt the aged through virtue and establish the five elders through primacy;

literal: the father is thereby made manifest, the elder brother thereby displayed."
idiomatic: the father shines forth, the elder brother stands clear."

literal: Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan and former Grand Herald Minggen—both suspended their lofty virtue in chariots and returned their fine measure in old age, so I honored the aged as three and served the five elders as five.
idiomatic: Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan and former Grand Herald Minggen—both hung up their virtue and retired in honor, so I made three for the aged and five for the elders.

literal: Though the three elders and five elders are not offices, and the oldest receive no salary, yet when the matter stands so high, special nurture should be added.
idiomatic: Though elders and five elders are not offices and the hoary receive no salary, the matter stands high and deserves special nurture.

literal: The three elders may receive salary of the senior lord; the five elders may eat the stipend of the prime origin minister.
idiomatic: The three elders may take a senior lord's stipend; the five elders a prime minister's pay.

literal: The flavor of food offered shall match the same standard."
idiomatic: The fare offered shall match the same standard."

literal: In year 17 Yuan fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him in person.
idiomatic: In year 17 Yuan fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him himself.

literal: When he died he was given posthumous title Duke Huan of Jing; burial with special rites, feathered canopy and martial pipes granted, yellow battle-axe lent, forty guards of the sword.
idiomatic: At his death he was titled Duke Huan of Jing; burial with special rites, feathered canopy and martial pipes, yellow battle-axe on loan, forty sword guards.

literal: His son Yi succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded.

literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, because Shanyang lay within the inner circuit, his title was changed to Duke of Boling Commandery.
idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang, Shanyang lying within the inner circuit, his house was retitled Duke of Boling.

literal: He died as Governor of Heng Province; posthumous title: Compliant.
idiomatic: He died as Governor of Heng; posthumous title: Compliant.

literal: Murong Baiyao was the great-great-grandson of Murong Huang.
idiomatic: Murong Baiyao was the great-great-grandson of Murong Huang.

literal: His father Ju held office and was famed for integrity and purity; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaodu.
idiomatic: His father Ju was famed in office for integrity and was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaodu.

literal: At death he was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title: Simple.
idiomatic: He ended as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title: Simple.

literal: Baiyao in youth was a clerk in the Secretariat; for honest uprightness he served in the palace.
idiomatic: In youth Baiyao was a Secretariat clerk; honest and upright, he served in the palace.

literal: He inherited the marquisate and was gradually promoted to Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: He inherited the rank and rose to Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan.

literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, he and Yi Hun together held court power; he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and advanced to Duke of Nanxiang.
idiomatic: At Wencheng's death he and Yi Hun seized court power; he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Nanxiang.

literal: Xue Andu, Governor of Xu Province in Song, and Bi Zhongjing, Governor of Yan, both surrendered their cities to the court; an edict ordered Grand General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan and Grand General Who Guards the East Kong Bogong to go.
idiomatic: Song's Governors Xue Andu of Xu and Bi Zhongjing of Yan surrendered their cities; the court ordered Wei Yuan, Grand General Who Guards the South, and Kong Bogong, Grand General Who Guards the East, to go.

literal: But Shen Zuan, Administrator of Dongping in Song, garrisoned Wuyan, and Fang Chongji, Inspector of Bing Province, held Doucheng, blocking and cutting off the king's envoys.
idiomatic: Yet Song's Dongping administrator Shen Zuan held Wuyan, and Bing Inspector Fang Chongji held Doucheng, blocking the king's envoys.

literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Baiyao was added bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs, and Grand General Who Campaigns South, and advanced to Duke of Shangdang.
idiomatic: At Huangxing's opening Baiyao was made bearer of the staff, military commander, and Grand General Who Campaigns South, and advanced to Duke of Shangdang.

literal: He encamped at Que'ao as rear for the armies.
idiomatic: He encamped at Que'ao as army reserve.

literal: Baiyao attacked Shen Zuan at Wuyan and took the eastern wall.
idiomatic: Baiyao attacked Shen Zuan at Wuyan and stormed the eastern wall.

literal: Zuan fled; Baiyao sent troops in pursuit and seized him.
idiomatic: Zuan fled; troops pursued and seized him.

literal: He turned to attack Doucheng.
idiomatic: He turned to attack Doucheng.

literal: The garrison chief of Feicheng, hearing the army had come, abandoned the city and fled; they seized three hundred thousand shi of grain.
idiomatic: Feicheng's garrison chief, hearing the army approach, fled; they took three hundred thousand shi of grain.

literal: He next descended and stormed the garrisons of Migou and Yuanmiao, gaining more than a hundred thousand hu of grain.
idiomatic: He next stormed Migou and Yuanmiao, gaining more than a hundred thousand hu of grain.

literal: Thus army provisions were ample.
idiomatic: Army provisions were ample thereafter.

literal: Earlier Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi had twice attacked Yuanmiao without success; within ten days Baiyao took four cities in succession, and his prestige shook Qi lands.
idiomatic: Earlier Pi Baozi of Huaiyang had twice failed against Yuanmiao; Baiyao took four cities in ten days, and his name shook Qi.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict praising him.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict of praise.

literal: Doucheng would not surrender; Baiyao let troops storm the walls and killed several hundred; Chongji fled by night.
idiomatic: Doucheng would not yield; Baiyao stormed the walls and killed hundreds; Chongji fled by night.

literal: Baiyao comforted the people; the common folk were drawn to him.
idiomatic: Baiyao comforted the people; the folk clung to him.

literal: He captured Chongji's mother and wife and treated them with ritual propriety.
idiomatic: He took Chongji's mother and wife and treated them with ritual propriety.

literal: Song sent the general Wu Xi intending to relieve Pengcheng; Grand General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan requested reinforcements, and Emperor Xiaowen ordered Baiyao to go.
idiomatic: Song sent Wu Xi to relieve Pengcheng; Wei Yuan asked for reinforcements, and Xiaowen ordered Baiyao there.
